title: Pull invoice details from email into a sheet and check them
summary: Mohamed Zaghloul shares an n8n workflow where Gemini reads PDF invoices from Gmail into Google Sheets, checks the totals, and flags low-confidence rows.
agent_role: The workflow watches a Gmail label, splits PDF attachments and has Gemini extract vendor, totals and line items into a fixed format. Code checks the math, flags uncertain rows and logs them to a sheet. A separate service checks bank account numbers. People review anything flagged.
what_they_did: A developer built a free n8n workflow that watches a Gmail label for invoice PDFs. Gemini pulls out the vendor, dates, totals and line items in a strict format. A code step checks that subtotal plus tax equals the total and flags low-confidence rows for review. Rows go into Google Sheets, and the email is marked read so it is not processed twice. He also shows how to add a separate check of bank account and tax numbers.
how_it_went: The author says setup takes about 10 minutes. He reports that a strict output format and doing the math in code made it more reliable.
worth_knowing: A commenter notes a valid bank number can still be a fraudster's. Treat any change to a vendor's account as needing review, and confirm it by a phone number you already have.
prompt: Build an n8n workflow that watches my Gmail for unread emails labelled [invoice label] with PDF attachments. For each PDF, extract the vendor, invoice number, dates, currency, subtotal, tax, total, line items and the vendor's bank account number in a strict format. Check in code that subtotal plus tax equals the total, allowing a cent of rounding. Flag uncertain rows as needs review, and flag any vendor whose bank account differs from earlier rows. Append each row to the Invoices tab of [Google Sheet name], then mark the email read. Show me the workflow plan first and wait for my approval before turning it on. Never pay or approve anything automatically.

curation.rationale: A detailed, reproducible multi-step workflow for pulling invoice details from email into a spreadsheet, with useful review safeguards. It is partly a pitch for the author's paid checking service and reports no usage results.
